answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use earned throughput caps: every new identity starts with a tiny transaction delta, only a few low-value exchanges per day, and its cap rises only after a history of settled, peer-attested work. Like a willow that grows slowly, trust cannot be bought in bulk: an attacker spawning thousands of fake identities gets thousands of useless tiny caps, while concentrating real work in one identity costs time and leaves a public trail. Nectar, the valuable rewards, flows only to identities whose cap was earned, so fakes starve while honest agents compound.
